mainTopic: Why a פסוק is needed to disqualify a טרפה as a קרבן, and the משנה's rules for a proper קמיצה of a מנחה
overview: The גמרא asks why the תורה needs a פסוק to rule a טרפה out as a קרבן. It tests several lines of logic. First, a מה הצד from מליקה and חלב ודם suggests a טרפה might be allowed on the מזבח; this is rejected because the מצוה is done that way in those cases. רב אשי and רב אחא סבא then argue over a צד השוה from a בעל מום and a יוצא דופן, which would forbid a טרפה even without a פסוק. The גמרא finally breaks it: their defects are visible, but a טרפה's defect usually is not, so the פסוק is needed. Next it asks why מן הבקר is needed when ממשקה ישראל and כל אשר יעבור תחת השבט also exclude a טרפה, and it shows that each פסוק covers a different case. A new משנה then lists who may not take the קמיצה, how it must be done, and what makes the קומץ too big or too small. The גמרא asks why the משנה names the מנחת חוטא separately, and answers that this is needed for רבי שמעון's view. It begins quoting his ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: כלאים is different because the מצוה requires it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from כלאים. כלאים is used in the כהן's clothing because the מצוה itself calls for it, and nothing like that applies to a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What can you learn from כלאים? Its מצוה is done exactly that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing away the earlier suggestion that כלאים proves a forbidden thing can still be used for holy service. It says כלאים is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof tried to say: כלאים is forbidden to a regular person but used in the כהן's clothing, so a טרפה should work for the מזבח too. The answer is that the clothing is commanded to be made of כלאים, so it is not a case of 'forbidden but allowed anyway.' No one is commanded to bring a טרפה, so the comparison falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures; here, wool and linen woven together
Its מצוה is done in exactly this way
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying כלאים stops being כלאים in the בגדי כהונה. It is still the same forbidden mixture. The point is that here the מצוה actually requires it, which makes it a unique case.

phrases.english: What is notable about diverse kinds?
phrases.notes: This refers to the כהן's belt, which is made of wool and linen mixed together.

phrases.english: That its מצוה is in this manner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the כלאים proof that the previous part of the סוגיא offered to explain why a פסוק is needed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects כלאים as a proof that something forbidden to a person could be allowed for holy use.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: כלאים in the בגדי כהונה is commanded, while a טרפה is never commanded for the מזבח.

steps.title: רב שישא builds a מה הצד argument: חלב ודם answer the מליקה problem
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי says the פסוק is needed because of a מה הצד argument. When someone objects that מליקה is different because its holiness is what makes it forbidden, he answers that חלב ודם prove the point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: the פסוק is needed because one could argue that the logic comes back through a מה הצד. If you say מליקה is different because its holiness is what forbids it, חלב ודם will prove otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא offers a new reason why the תורה needs a פסוק to rule out a טרפה. He begins building a two-source argument, starting with how חלב ודם cover the weakness of מליקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird killed by מליקה is only forbidden because of the holy service that was done to it, so you might say the holiness that forbids it also permits it on the מזבח. חלב ודם, however, are forbidden to a person even before they become holy, and they still go on the מזבח. So 'its holiness forbids it' cannot be the full reason something forbidden is allowed on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: A proof built from the shared feature of two sources
Killing a bird offering by pinching its neck with the fingernail
Its holiness is what makes it forbidden
Forbidden fats and blood, which are placed on the מזבח
They will prove

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic way the גמרא explains why a פסוק is needed: it shows that logic alone might have led to the opposite conclusion.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
Because it can be said,
Let the reasoning return and come through a 'common element' argument:
If you ask: what is notable about pinching?
That its sanctity is what prohibits it,
Fat and blood will prove otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the כלאים approach fails, רב שישא offers a different explanation for why the פסוק is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that logic could have permitted a טרפה, so a פסוק is needed to forbid it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the earlier proofs were rejected, we might think no פסוק was needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מה הצד argument from מליקה and חלב ודם could have permitted a טרפה.

steps.title: מליקה answers the weakness of חלב ודם
steps.stepSummary: If you object that חלב ודם are different because they come from an animal that is permitted, מליקה proves otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say חלב ודם are different because they come from something generally permitted, מליקה will prove otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא continues his argument. Now he shows how מליקה covers the weakness of חלב ודם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב ודם come from a kosher animal whose meat is permitted, so you might say only small parts of a permitted animal can be allowed on the מזבח. But a bird killed by מליקה is completely forbidden to eat, and it still goes on the מזבח. So 'coming from something permitted' is not the deciding factor either.

keyTerms.meaning: From something that is, in general, permitted
Will prove (feminine form, referring to מליקה)

phrases.english: If you ask: what is notable about fat and blood?
That they come from something generally permitted,
Pinching will prove otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְחֵלֶב וָדָם, שֶׁכֵּן בָּאִים מִכְּלַל הֶיתֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second half of the back-and-forth: each source covers the other's weakness.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Answers the weakness of the second source using the first source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חלב ודם might be special because they come from a permitted animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: מליקה is entirely forbidden and still goes on the מזבח, so that difference does not matter.

steps.title: The common element: forbidden to people, permitted to the מזבח, so a טרפה too
steps.stepSummary: Neither source is exactly like the other, but both are forbidden to an ordinary person and allowed on the מזבח. So a טרפה should be allowed on the מזבח as well, and that is why a פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has come back around. This case is not like that one, and that case is not like this one. What they share is that they are forbidden to an ordinary person and permitted to the מזבח. So I will also bring a טרפה: even though it is forbidden to an ordinary person, it should be permitted to the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא finishes his מה הצד argument. He concludes that logic alone would have permitted a טרפה on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source's weakness has been covered by the other, so only their shared feature is left: forbidden to a person, permitted on the מזבח. A טרפה also has the first half, since it is forbidden to a person. So the argument says it should get the second half too. That is exactly why the תורה needed a פסוק to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument has come back around
The feature of this case is not like the feature of that one
The common element
An ordinary person (as opposed to the holy realm)
'The Most High', meaning the מזבח and holy use

steps.whatToRemember: A מה הצד works when two sources each fix the other's weakness. What remains is their shared feature, and that feature is then applied to the new case.

phrases.english: And the reasoning has come back around,
The feature of this one is not like the feature of that one,
And the feature of that one is not like the feature of this one,
The common element between them is
That they are forbidden to an ordinary person and permitted to the Most High,
So I will also bring a tereifa:
Even though it is forbidden to an ordinary person,
It should be permitted to the Most High,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין, לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties together the two halves from steps 2 and 3 into the final conclusion of the מה הצד.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב שישא concludes that logic alone, through a מה הצד, would have permitted a טרפה on the מזבח, so the פסוק is needed. Step 5 rejects this.

steps.title: Their common element is also that the מצוה is done that way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב שישא's argument. מליקה and חלב ודם share another feature: the מצוה is done exactly that way. That does not apply to a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What can you learn from their common element? In both, the מצוה is done in exactly that way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב שישא's argument using the same idea that knocked down כלאים in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מליקה is the commanded way to kill a bird offering, and חלב ודם are commanded to be offered on the מזבח. So their shared feature is not just 'forbidden but allowed'. It is 'commanded for the מזבח'. A טרפה is never commanded, so it cannot be learned from them, and the question of why a פסוק is needed comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Its מצוה is done in exactly this way

steps.whatToRemember: A מה הצד can be broken by finding a second feature that both sources share but the new case lacks. Here that feature is 'its מצוה is done this way'.

phrases.english: What is notable about their common element?
That its מצוה is done in this manner!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן שֶׁכֵּן מִצְוָתָהּ בְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of רב שישא's מה הצד in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole מה הצד argument that would permit a טרפה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources share a feature a טרפה lacks: they are commanded for the מזבח.

steps.title: רב אשי: the reasoning from a blemished animal is flawed from the start
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a new reason why a פסוק is needed. The קל וחומר from a בעל מום fails, because with blemishes the תורה treated the כהן who offers like the animal that is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: we need the פסוק because the reasoning is flawed from the very start. Where are you learning it from? From a בעל מום. But a בעל מום is special: there, the תורה made those who offer like what is offered.
steps.whatsHappening: After the earlier answers were knocked down, רב אשי offers a fresh reason why the תורה needed a פסוק to rule a טרפה unfit for the מזבח. He says the basic קל וחומר never worked in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר went like this: a בעל מום is allowed to an ordinary person yet forbidden on the מזבח, so a טרפה, which is forbidden even to an ordinary person, should surely be forbidden on the מזבח. רב אשי attacks the source case itself. Blemishes are special because they disqualify both the כהן and the animal. That is not true of טרפה, since a כהן who is a טרפה may still serve. So the פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The reasoning has a flaw from its very starting point
A refutation; a point that breaks a comparison
An animal (or person) with a physical blemish
Those who offer are treated like what is offered (a blemished כהן is disqualified just like a blemished animal)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
because one can say:
the reasoning is flawed from its very start.
From where are you bringing it?
phrases.notes: "It" is the rule that a טרפה is unfit for the מזבח, which we were trying to learn through a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: From a blemished animal.
What about a blemished animal?
It is special, since there the Torah made those who offer like what is offered.
phrases.notes: A כהן with a blemish can't serve, just like a blemished animal can't be offered. Nothing like that is true for טרפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר: מֵעִיקָּרָא דְּדִינָא פִּרְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב שישא's answer is rejected in step 5, רב אשי offers a new answer to the same question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Breaking the base קל וחומר by finding a special feature in the source case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a פסוק, we could learn by קל וחומר from a בעל מום that a טרפה is unfit for the מזבח, so the פסוק would be unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר fails because a בעל מום has the feature of מקריבין כקריבין, so a פסוק is needed.

steps.title: רב אחא סבא: a יוצא דופן proves otherwise
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא סבא challenges רב אשי. A יוצא דופן has no מקריבין כקריבין rule, yet it is allowed to an ordinary person and forbidden on the מזבח. So that feature is not what matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא סבא said to רב אשי: let a יוצא דופן prove the point. With it, the Torah did not make those who offer like what is offered, and yet it is allowed to an ordinary person and forbidden on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא סבא attacks רב אשי's answer. He brings a case that lacks the special feature רב אשי pointed to, yet still follows the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal born by caesarean cannot be offered, but a כהן born that way may serve. So there is no מקריבין כקריבין here. Still, such an animal may be eaten but not offered. This shows the קל וחומר can stand without that feature, which brings back the question of why a פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born through the side of its mother (caesarean section)
"Will prove": a case brought to show that a proposed distinction does not matter
An ordinary person (for eating)
"The One on High": the מזבח, for offering

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא סָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha Sava said to Rav Ashi:
An animal born by caesarean section will prove it,
for with it the Torah did not make those who offer like what is offered,
phrases.notes: A כהן born this way may still serve, even though the animal can't be offered.

phrases.english: and yet it is permitted to an ordinary person and forbidden for the Most High.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's distinction from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the feature of מקריבין כקריבין breaks the קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A יוצא דופן lacks that feature yet is still allowed to an ordinary person and forbidden on the מזבח. So the קל וחומר can be built from it instead, and the פסוק would again seem unnecessary.

steps.title: רב אשי: a יוצא דופן is not holy as a בכור
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that a יוצא דופן is also special, because it does not get בכור holiness. So it cannot serve as a base for learning about a טרפה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a יוצא דופן? It is special, because it does not become holy as a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends his answer. He points out a special feature of the יוצא דופן, so the קל וחומר cannot be built from it either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A firstborn animal born by caesarean does not receive the holiness of a בכור. A firstborn that is a טרפה does receive it. Since the יוצא דופן is weaker in holiness in a way the טרפה is not, we cannot learn the טרפה from it. Without the פסוק we might have allowed a טרפה on the מזבח, so the פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn status, which makes a firstborn animal holy
Holy; given sacred status

steps.whatToRemember: Each source case for the קל וחומר has its own special feature. A בעל מום has מקריבין כקריבין, and a יוצא דופן is not holy as a בכור. So we cannot learn about a טרפה by logic alone, and a פסוק is needed.

phrases.english: What about an animal born by caesarean section?
It is special, since it is not holy with firstborn status.
phrases.notes: A firstborn born this way doesn't become a בכור, while a firstborn that is a טרפה does.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן, שֶׁכֵּן אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ בִּבְכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא סבא's challenge from step 7 and protects רב אשי's answer from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing out a special feature in the challenger's case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר could be built from a יוצא דופן, which has no מקריבין כקריבין feature.
steps.terutzMaskana: A יוצא דופן is not holy as a בכור, unlike a טרפה, so it cannot serve as the base. The פסוק remains necessary.

steps.title: Each case covers the other's weak spot
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא סבא answers back: a בעל מום proves the בכור feature does not matter, and a יוצא דופן proves the מקריבין כקריבין feature does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blemished animal proves it. And if you ask what is special about a blemished animal, that with it the Torah treated those who offer like those that are offered, then one born by caesarean proves it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא סבא rejects רב אשי's answer from step 8. He plays the two cases against each other, so that neither special feature can block the learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said a יוצא דופן is special because it gets no בכור holiness. רב אחא סבא answers that a blemished בכור does get that holiness and is still forbidden on the מזבח. If someone says a בעל מום is special because of מקריבין כקריבין, a יוצא דופן has no such rule, as step 7 showed.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove; another case shows that a supposed difference does not matter
An animal with a blemish, which may not be offered on the מזבח
Those who offer are treated like what is offered; a blemished כהן is disqualified, like a blemished animal
An animal born by caesarean section

steps.confusionAlert: This is a back-and-forth pattern. Each time someone says 'this case is special,' the other case is used to show that the special feature is not what matters.

phrases.english: A blemished animal will prove it,
What about a blemished animal?
For with it [the Torah] made
those who offer like those that are offered.
One born by caesarean section will prove it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's answer in step 8 that יוצא דופן is special
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the lack of בכור holiness makes יוצא דופן special
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each special feature is found missing in the other case, which is still forbidden on the מזבח, so neither feature is the real reason

steps.title: The common feature: a טרפה should be forbidden even without a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא סבא concludes with a צד השוה: both cases are allowed to an ordinary person and forbidden on the מזבח, so all the more so a טרפה, which is forbidden even to an ordinary person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reasoning has come back around. This case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they share is that they are allowed to an ordinary person and forbidden for the Most High. All the more so a טרפה, which is forbidden to an ordinary person, should be forbidden for the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא סבא sums up his argument. He builds a צד השוה and concludes that a טרפה is forbidden on the מזבח through logic alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither case alone works, because each has its own special feature. But both share one thing: they are allowed to eat and forbidden on the מזבח. A טרפה is stricter, since even a regular person may not eat it, so it should surely be forbidden on the מזבח. If so, the פסוק seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The reasoning has come back around to a combined proof
This case is not like that one; each source has its own special feature
The common feature shared by two sources, used to prove a third case
An ordinary person, as opposed to the מזבח
The Most High, meaning the מזבח and offerings
All the more so

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the strongest form of the challenge. If it holds, the פסוק that forbids a טרפה on the מזבח would have nothing to teach.

phrases.english: And the reasoning has come back around,
The feature of this is not like the feature of that
and the feature of that is not like the feature of this,
The common feature between them
is that they are allowed to an ordinary person
and forbidden for the Most High.
And all the more so a טרפה,
which is forbidden to an ordinary person,
should be forbidden for the Most High.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין, לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אחא סבא's argument begun in step 9
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אחא סבא concludes that, through a צד השוה of בעל מום and יוצא דופן, a טרפה should be forbidden on the מזבח without a פסוק. Step 11 rejects this.

steps.title: A טרפה was permitted in some case, unlike the others
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the צד השוה: בעל מום and יוצא דופן were never permitted out of their rule, but a טרפה was, so a פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about their common feature? They were never permitted out of their general rule. Can you say the same about a טרפה, which was permitted out of its general rule?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finds a weakness that both sources share, which a טרפה does not have. That breaks the צד השוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צד השוה fails if both sources share an extra strict feature that the new case lacks. Blemished and caesarean animals are never allowed on the מזבח. A טרפה does have a case where it is allowed, so it cannot be learned from them, and the פסוק is needed again.

keyTerms.meaning: Was permitted out of its general rule; there is a case where the usual ban does not apply
An animal with a fatal injury or defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: What about the common feature between them?
For they were never permitted out of their general rule.
Will you say the same about a טרפה,
which was permitted out of its general rule?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the צד השוה argument of step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The צד השוה of בעל מום and יוצא דופן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources are never permitted, while a טרפה has an exception, so the sources are stricter than the case being learned

steps.title: Which permitted טרפה? A blemished bird is also permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks what 'permitted טרפה' means. If it means מליקה of a bird עולה, a blemished bird is also permitted, so בעל מום has the same exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: This טרפה that was permitted out of its rule, what is it? If you say it is מליקה of a bird burnt offering for the Most High, a blemished animal is also permitted when it comes to birds. Being unblemished and male is required for animals, but not for birds!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges רב אשי's distinction from step 11. He shows that a בעל מום also has an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only obvious permitted טרפה is a bird offering killed by מליקה, which makes it a טרפה, yet it goes on the מזבח. But blemishes do not disqualify birds at all. So בעל מום was also 'permitted out of its rule,' and רב אשי's difference falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Killing a bird offering by pinching the neck with the כהן's fingernail
A bird burnt offering
It was indeed permitted
Being unblemished and male, a requirement for animal offerings

steps.confusionAlert: מליקה counts as making the bird a טרפה, since it is not proper שחיטה. That is why it is the example of a 'permitted טרפה.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
This טרפה that was permitted out of its general rule,
what is it?
If you say it is the pinching
of a bird burnt offering for the Most High,
then a blemished one too
was indeed permitted with birds,
Being unblemished and male applies to animals,
and there is no unblemished-and-male requirement for birds!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's distinction in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that only a טרפה was permitted out of its rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the permitted טרפה is מליקה of birds, then בעל מום is also permitted for birds, so both sources were also permitted out of their rule

steps.title: The second meaning of 'permitted טרפה' also fails
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps 'permitted טרפה' means that a bird חטאת killed by מליקה may be eaten by כהנים. But that does not work, because כהנים only eat from what belongs to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe you mean that a bird חטאת killed by pinching is permitted to the כהנים. But that doesn't help: the כהנים eat only from the 'table of the Most High.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא keeps challenging רב אשי. He tries a second meaning of 'a טרפה was permitted' and shows that this one fails too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird killed by מליקה is like a טרפה for an ordinary person, yet כהנים may eat a חטאת העוף killed this way. But the כהנים only get it because the מזבח got it first. So this is not a separate permission for a טרפה, and רב אשי's difference between טרפה and the other two cases falls apart again.

keyTerms.meaning: Killing a bird קרבן by pinching its neck with the כהן's fingernail instead of slaughtering it with a knife
A bird brought as a sin offering. Its meat is eaten by the כהנים
'The table of the Most High.' The כהנים get their share only through what was given to the מזבח

phrases.english: Rather, the pinching of a bird sin offering
is permitted to the priests,
but the priests receive from the table of the Most High.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 12's attack by testing the second possible meaning of 'permitted טרפה'
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim (step 11) that a טרפה was permitted out of its rule, unlike a בעל מום and a יוצא דופן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהנים' right to eat a pinched חטאת העוף comes only from the מזבח's permission. So it is not an independent permission of a טרפה, and it cannot set a טרפה apart from the other cases.

steps.title: A new refutation: a טרפה's defect is not visible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא breaks the צד השוה a different way. A בעל מום and a יוצא דופן both have a noticeable defect, but a טרפה often does not. So you cannot learn a טרפה from them, and a פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, refute it like this: the shared feature of those two cases is that their defect can be seen. Can you say the same about a טרפה, whose defect cannot be seen? That is why a פסוק was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב אשי's reason failed, the גמרא gives a new reason why the צד השוה does not work. This finally explains why the פסוק is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צד השוה only works if the shared feature of the two sources also applies to the new case. Both a בעל מום and a יוצא דופן have a defect you can see or know about. A טרפה is often damaged inside where no one can see it. Maybe the תורה only disqualifies obvious defects, so we cannot learn a טרפה from them without a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The common feature of two sources, used to learn a law for a third case
A defect that can be noticed or seen
A פסוק was needed
Refute; break the argument

steps.whatToRemember: The final reason a פסוק is needed for טרפה: a בעל מום and a יוצא דופן have visible defects, but a טרפה's defect is usually hidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long back-and-forth from earlier steps. It shows that the פסוק about טרפה is not extra, because logic alone could not teach it.

phrases.english: Rather, refute it like this:
What about the common element between them,
since their defect is noticeable?
phrases.notes: "Their" means the בעל מום and the יוצא דופן from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: Will you say the same about a tereifa,
whose defect is not noticeable?
Because of that, a verse was needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב אשי's failed refutation with a new one that works
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinction that breaks the צד השוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The צד השוה of בעל מום and יוצא דופן would teach a קל וחומר that a טרפה is disqualified, so the פסוק would be extra
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sources have a visible defect and a טרפה does not, so the קל וחומר fails and the פסוק is needed

steps.title: Isn't the טרפה rule learned from ממשקה ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a new question: is the rule that a טרפה cannot be a קרבן really learned from this פסוק? It is already learned from ממשקה ישראל, which teaches that a קרבן must come from what is permitted to a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is the טרפה rule learned from here? It is learned from there: 'From the well-watered pastures of Israel,' meaning only from what is permitted to Israel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge. It points to a different פסוק that already seems to teach that a טרפה cannot be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 just showed that a פסוק is needed. Now the גמרא asks why it must be this פסוק, since ממשקה ישראל already excludes anything a Jew may not eat, and a טרפה is forbidden to eat. The pressure moves from 'why a פסוק?' to 'why this פסוק?'

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived; it comes out from
'From the well-watered pastures of Israel,' a פסוק in יחזקאל
Only from what is permitted for a Jew to eat

phrases.english: But is the law of a tereifa derived from here?
It is derived from there:
"From the well-watered pastures of Israel"
meaning from what is permitted to Israel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving a פסוק is needed, the גמרא questions whether this is the right פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: The source given for disqualifying a טרפה as a קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק already excludes anything forbidden to a Jew, so the טרפה rule should come from there and not from here.

steps.title: Or from 'whatever passes under the rod'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another possible source for the טרפה rule: the פסוק about מעשר בהמה, 'whatever passes under the rod.' A טרפה does not pass, so it is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: It can also be learned from 'Whatever passes under the rod': this leaves out a טרפה, which does not pass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second alternative source, which makes the question from step 15 even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two other פסוקים that already seem to exclude a טרפה: ממשקה ישראל and the מעשר בהמה פסוק. So it is even harder to see why the original פסוק, מן הבקר, is needed for this. Steps 17 and 18 answer this with צריכי: each פסוק covers a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: The rod used to count animals for מעשר בהמה
The animal tithe: every tenth animal that passes under the rod becomes holy
Excluding; leaving out

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an answer to step 15. It is a second alternative source, which adds to the question.

phrases.english: From "Whatever passes under the rod"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:32, about counting animals for מעשר בהמה.

phrases.english: it is derived, excluding a tereifa, which does not pass under it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבוֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second alternative source to the challenge in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The source given for disqualifying a טרפה as a קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מעשר בהמה פסוק also excludes a טרפה, so the original פסוק seems even less needed for this rule.

steps.title: Why ממשקה ישראל alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that all the sources are needed. ממשקה ישראל alone would only exclude an animal that was never fit, so כל אשר יעבור is needed for an animal that was once fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the פסוקים are needed. If we only had ממשקה ישראל, I would think it excludes only an animal that was never fit, like ערלה and כלאי הכרם. But an animal that was once fit, I might think, stays fit. So the Torah wrote 'whatever passes under the rod.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the questions from steps 15 and 16 by saying 'they are all needed.' It starts by showing why ממשקה ישראל by itself would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ממשקה ישראל is compared to ערלה and כלאי הכרם, which were never allowed at all. So that פסוק alone would only exclude a טרפה that was never fit, such as one born a טרפה. The פסוק of מעשר בהמה is needed to teach that even an animal that was fit at first and later became a טרפה is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed. Each source teaches something the others do not.
I would have thought. This is the mistaken idea we would have had without the extra פסוק.
A time when it was fit
Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
Forbidden mixed plantings in a vineyard

steps.confusionAlert: צריכי does not mean the גמרא is dropping its question. It means the answer is that all three sources stay, because each covers a different case.

phrases.english: They are necessary,
phrases.notes: He means all three sources from the last steps are needed.

phrases.english: because if it were only from 'the well-watered pastures of Israel'
I would have said it comes to exclude

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּלֹא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר,
phrases.english: only where it never had a time of fitness,
similar to orla and diverse kinds in a vineyard,
but if it had a time of fitness,
I might say it should be fit,
so the Merciful One wrote 'whatever passes under the rod.'

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכִי, דְּאִי מִ״מַּשְׁקֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל״ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 15 and 16 by showing that each פסוק is needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source covers a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ממשקה ישראל alone excludes only an animal that was never fit
steps.terutzMaskana: כל אשר יעבור is needed to exclude an animal that was once fit and later became a טרפה

steps.title: Why כל אשר יעבור alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק of מעשר alone would only exclude an animal that became a טרפה before it was made holy. מן הבקר is needed for one that became a טרפה after it was made holy. So all three are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written only 'whatever passes under the rod,' I would think it excludes only an animal that became a טרפה and was made holy afterward, like מעשר. But if it was made holy first and only later became a טרפה, it was fit when it became holy, so I might say it stays fit. So the Torah wrote 'from the herd.' All of them are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It shows why the מעשר פסוק is not enough by itself, and why מן הבקר is also needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר is about the moment an animal becomes holy, so that פסוק would only stop a טרפה from becoming holy in the first place. An animal that was already holy and fit, and only later became a טרפה, needs מן הבקר to make it פסול. So each of the three sources has its own job.

keyTerms.meaning: It became a טרפה
He made it holy and set it aside for the מקדש
The tithe of animals, where every tenth animal passing under the rod becomes holy
Fit

steps.whatToRemember: There are three sources for 'a טרפה cannot be a קרבן.' ממשקה ישראל covers an animal that was never fit. כל אשר יעבור covers one that was fit, then became a טרפה, and was made holy afterward. מן הבקר covers one that was made holy first and became a טרפה later.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'whatever passes under the rod,'
I would have said it comes to exclude
only where it became a טרפה and afterward he made it holy,
similar to the tithe.
But if he made it holy and afterward it became a טרפה,
since at the time he made it holy it was fit,
I might say it should be fit.
So the Merciful One wrote 'from the herd,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:3. This is the פסוק the discussion started with.

phrases.english: so they are all necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״כׇּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבוֹר״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the צריכותא started in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source covers a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כל אשר יעבור alone excludes only an animal that became a טרפה before it was made holy
steps.terutzMaskana: מן הבקר teaches that even an animal that became a טרפה after it was made holy is פסול

steps.title: The משנה lists people and positions that make the קמיצה פסול
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. Any מנחה, including a מנחת חוטא, is פסול if the handful was taken by a זר, an אונן, a טבול יום, and so on, or by a כהן standing in the wrong way.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sinner's מנחה and every other מנחה are פסול if the handful was taken by: a non-כהן, an אונן, a טבול יום, a כהן missing his בגדי כהונה, a כהן who still needs to bring his atonement קרבן, one who did not wash his hands and feet, an uncircumcised כהן, a טמא כהן, a כהן who was sitting, or one standing on vessels, on an animal, or on another person's feet.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins here. It lists who cannot do the קמיצה and in what positions it cannot be done. If any of these is wrong, the מנחה is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קמיצה is treated like any other main עבודה in the מקדש. So everyone who is not allowed to do עבודה, like a זר, a טמא, or a כהן without his special clothes, makes it פסול. The כהן must also stand directly on the floor of the עזרה, not on anything in between.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner's מנחה, brought by a poor person for certain sins
Taking a handful of the flour of a מנחה with three fingers to burn on the מזבח
A non-כהן
A mourner on the day a close relative died, before the burial
A person who went to the מקוה today and is waiting for nightfall to become fully טהור
A person who still needs to bring a קרבן to finish becoming טהור

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up טבול יום and מחוסר כפורים. Both already went to the מקוה. The טבול יום is waiting for night, and the מחוסר כפורים is waiting to bring his קרבן.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Both the meal offering of a sinner
and all other meal offerings,
whose handful was taken by a non-priest,
an acute mourner, one who immersed that day,
one lacking the priestly garments, one lacking atonement,
one who did not wash his hands and feet,
phrases.notes: This means washing from the כיור (the basin) before doing עבודה.

phrases.english: an uncircumcised one, an impure one, one sitting,
one standing on vessels,
on an animal,
or on the feet of another person: it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֶחָד מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא וְאֶחָד כׇּל הַמְּנָחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the טרפה discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קמיצה of any מנחה done by someone who cannot do עבודה, or done in a wrong position, makes the מנחה פסול

steps.title: Taking the handful with the left hand
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a קמיצה done with the left hand is פסול. בן בתירא says the כהן puts the handful back and takes it again with his right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he took the handful with his left hand, the מנחה is פסול. בן בתירא says: he puts the handful back and takes it again with his right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case, a קמיצה done with the left hand. It brings a מחלוקת about whether the מנחה can be fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the קמיצה must be done with the right hand. The תנא קמא holds that a left-hand קמיצה ruins the whole מנחה. בן בתירא holds that it can be fixed: the handful goes back into the flour, and the כהן takes it again properly with his right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Left hand
Right hand
He should return it, meaning put the handful back into the מנחה
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key question for the גמרא that follows: can a קמיצה done the wrong way be fixed by doing it again, or is the מנחה ruined for good?

phrases.english: If he took the handful with the left hand, it is unfit,
Ben Beteira says: He must return it
phrases.notes: He puts the handful back into the vessel with the rest of the flour.

phrases.english: and again take the handful with the right hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָמַץ בִּשְׂמֹאל – פָּסוּל, בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with another way the קמיצה can be done wrong, and adds a מחלוקת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says a left-hand קמיצה makes the מנחה פסול. בן בתירא says the handful is returned and taken again with the right hand.

steps.title: Something foreign comes up in the handful
steps.stepSummary: If a pebble, salt grain, or bit of לבונה comes up in the קמיצה, the מנחה is פסול, because a handful that is too big or too small is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the כהן took the handful and a pebble, a grain of salt, or a small piece of frankincense came up in his hand, the offering is פסול. This is because the Sages said that a handful that is too big or too small is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case of a bad קמיצה: something that is not flour comes up in the כהן's hand. It says the מנחה is פסול and gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The foreign object takes up room in the handful, so there is less flour than a full קומץ. That makes it a handful that is חסר, too small. The משנה ties this case to a wider rule: the קומץ must be exactly the right amount, not more and not less.

keyTerms.meaning: He took the handful of flour from the מנחה
A small stone or pebble
A small bit or pinch of frankincense
A handful that is too big or too small

phrases.english: If he took the handful and a pebble came up in his hand,
or a grain of salt,
or a pinch of frankincense, it is unfit,
because they said:
A handful that is too big or too small is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of ways a קמיצה becomes פסול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A handful containing a pebble, salt, or frankincense is פסול, because a קומץ that is too big or too small is פסול.

steps.title: What counts as too big and too small
steps.stepSummary: Too big means the handful is overflowing. Too small means it was taken with only the fingertips.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a handful that is too big? One where he took it overflowing. What is too small? One where he took it with just the tips of his fingers.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines the two words it just used, יתר and חסר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proper קומץ is taken with the fingers closed over the palm. If flour spills out over the top, the handful is too big. If he only pinches with his fingertips, it is too small.

keyTerms.meaning: Overflowing, bulging out of the hand
The tips of his fingers

steps.whatToRemember: The קומץ must be an exact, normal handful. Too much, too little, or mixed with something that is not flour all make the מנחה פסול.

phrases.english: And which is too big? One where he took the handful overflowing,
and too small: one where he took the handful with the tips of his fingers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the terms יתר and חסר used in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An overflowing handful is יתר. A fingertip handful is חסר.

steps.title: Why mention the מנחת חוטא separately?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה said 'both a מנחת חוטא and all מנחות' when it could simply have said 'all מנחות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did the משנה need to say 'both the sinner's מנחה and all other מנחות'? It should just say 'all the מנחות where a זר or an אונן took the handful'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and questions the wording of the משנה from step 19. It asks why the מנחת חוטא is named on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All the מנחות' already includes the מנחת חוטא, so naming it looks extra. The גמרא assumes every word of a משנה is there for a reason, so it wants to know what this extra mention teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? A question about something that looks extra
The flour offering of a poor sinner, brought without oil or לבונה
Let it teach, meaning the משנה should have said it this way

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why do I need it to teach
'Both the sinner's meal offering and all the meal offerings'?
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of the משנה from step 19.

phrases.english: Let it teach: 'All the meal offerings
whose handful was taken by a non-כהן or a mourner'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the opening line of the משנה from step 19 to question its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'אחד מנחת חוטא ואחד כל המנחות' in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'All the מנחות' already covers the מנחת חוטא, so mentioning it separately seems extra.

steps.title: It was needed for רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the separate mention of מנחת חוטא is needed according to רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer: the extra words are there because of רבי שמעון's opinion. Next it will quote רבי שמעון's ברייתא to show why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer says that according to רבי שמעון, the מנחת חוטא is special in some way. Without its own mention, one might think the usual rules do not apply to it. The ברייתא that follows lays out his view.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: why the sinner's offering is kept plain
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the sinner's מנחה should really need oil and לבונה so the sinner does not gain. It doesn't, so that his offering won't look fancy. Likewise a חטאת חלב should really need נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי שמעון said: By right, the sinner's מנחה should need oil and frankincense, so that the sinner should not come out ahead. So why does it not need them? So that his offering should not be beautiful. And by right, the sin offering for eating forbidden fat should need wine libations,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's ברייתא to explain his view of the sinner's offering. The quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could argue that leaving out oil and לבונה makes things easier and cheaper for the sinner, as if he 'profits' from sinning. רבי שמעון says the real reason is the opposite: a sinner's offering should not be dressed up and beautiful. He then applies the same idea to the חטאת for eating חלב.

keyTerms.meaning: By right, logically it should be
Gains, comes out ahead
Beautiful, of fancy quality
The חטאת brought for eating forbidden fat by mistake
Wine libations poured with some offerings

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying the sinner's offering really needs oil and לבונה. He says that is what logic would suggest, and then explains why the halacha leaves them out.

steps.raayaObject: The claim that the מנחת חוטא has a special status according to רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון explaining why the sinner's offering lacks oil and לבונה, and why a חטאת חלב would logically need נסכים.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי שמעון's idea that a sinner's offering is kept plain explains why the משנה needed to name the מנחת חוטא by itself.
